subject: Epigenetic aging was slowest in a 6.4-to-7.8-hour sleep window
script: From Agewell Brief: Epigenetic aging was slowest in a 6.4-to-7.8-hour sleep window. A new analysis links sleep duration to epigenetic aging, with a sweet spot that echoes ancestral patterns and the restorative biology first mapped by Kleitman. Optimal sleep range: 6.4–7.8 hours per night. Both short and long sleep may accelerate epigenetic aging. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
